docs.title: Mocked Subject (mocked_subject)
docs.text:
What it is

A test file mocks the module its subject under test is imported from, so the test exercises the double instead of the code — mock collaborators, keep the subject real.

Why it's bad

A test that replaces the module it claims to test checks the double's canned answer; it stays green when the real code breaks.

Example

PythonJS / TS MediumHigh

Flags a mock whose module resolves to the import a test calls its subject through.

Problem

from unittest.mock import patch

from shop import pricing


@patch("shop.pricing.quote", return_value=42)
def test_quote(mocked):
    assert pricing.quote(2) == 42

Proposed fix

Patch the collaborators the subject calls, or patch with wraps= to keep the real function.

from shop import pricing


def test_quote(mocker):
    mocker.patch("shop.pricing.fetch_rate", return_value=2)
    assert pricing.quote(2) == 4

Also flags a mocked module named like the test file, and patches of an attribute on an imported object the test calls.

Problem

from unittest.mock import patch

from shop.pricing import Pricing


def test_quote():
    with patch.object(Pricing, "rate", return_value=2):
        assert Pricing().quote(2) == 4

Proposed fix

Patch the collaborators the subject calls, or patch with wraps= to keep the real function.

from shop import pricing


def test_quote(mocker):
    mocker.patch("shop.pricing.fetch_rate", return_value=2)
    assert pricing.quote(2) == 4
MediumHigh

Flags a mock whose module resolves to the import a test calls its subject through.

Problem

import { quote } from "./pricing";

vi.mock("./pricing", () => ({ quote: vi.fn(() => 42) }));

it("quotes", () => {
  expect(quote({ qty: 2 })).toBe(42);
});

Proposed fix

Mock the collaborators the subject imports, or keep the real module with importActual / importOriginal.

import { quote } from "./pricing";

vi.mock("./rates", () => ({ fetchRate: vi.fn(() => 1.5) }));

it("quotes", () => {
  expect(quote({ qty: 2 })).toBe(3);
});

Also flags a mocked module named like the test file, and patches of an attribute on an imported object the test calls.

Problem

// pricing.example.test.ts: the mocked module shares the test file's name.
import { render } from "./receipt";

vi.mock("./pricing");

it("renders the receipt", () => {
  expect(render({ qty: 2 })).toContain("4");
});

Proposed fix

Mock the collaborators the subject imports, or keep the real module with importActual / importOriginal.

import { quote } from "./pricing";

vi.mock("./rates", () => ({ fetchRate: vi.fn(() => 1.5) }));

it("quotes", () => {
  expect(quote({ qty: 2 })).toBe(3);
});

docs.title: Redundant Wrapper Chain (redundant_wrapper_chain)
docs.text:
What it is

A local function forwards arguments unchanged without adding behavior — remove the wrapper or allow a deliberate depth in configuration.

Why it's bad

An unchanged forwarding layer adds indirection without behavior and makes navigation harder.

Example

PythonJS / TS

Problem

def normalize(value: int) -> int:
    return value + 1


def middle(value: int) -> int:
    return normalize(value)


def outer(value: int) -> int:
    return middle(value)


result = outer(2)

Proposed fix

Remove pass-through functions, or raise max_depth when a deliberate boundary is worth keeping.

def normalize(value: int) -> int:
    return value + 1


result = normalize(2)

Problem

function normalize(value: number): number {
  return value + 1;
}

function middle(value: number): number {
  return normalize(value);
}

function outer(value: number): number {
  return middle(value);
}

const result = outer(2);
console.log(result);

Proposed fix

Remove pass-through functions, or raise max_depth when a deliberate boundary is worth keeping.

function normalize(value: number): number {
  return value + 1;
}

const result = normalize(2);
console.log(result);

Tune It

docs.title: Shipped Stub (stub_shipped)
docs.text:
What it is

A production function whose whole body is a placeholder (pass, raise NotImplementedError, a "not implemented" throw) — it fails the first caller who reaches it.

Why it's bad

Scaffolding written for later ships as a function that only fails, and the first user on that path hits the error at runtime. Unreferenced stubs are also reported as dead code. Keep deliberate scaffolding folders out with [smells] exclude.

Example

PythonJS / TS

Problem

def export_ledger(org_id: str) -> bytes:
    raise NotImplementedError


report = export_ledger("acme")

Proposed fix

Implement the function, delete it with its callers, or declare it with @abstractmethod on an ABC/Protocol.

def export_ledger(org_id: str) -> bytes:
    return f"ledger,{org_id}\n".encode()


report = export_ledger("acme")

Problem

export async function exportLedger(orgId: string): Promise<Blob> {
  // TODO: implement CSV export
  throw new Error("not implemented");
}

Proposed fix

Implement the function, delete it with its callers, or declare it abstract or as an interface member. Tune the thrown messages with markers.

export async function exportLedger(orgId: string): Promise<Blob> {
  return new Blob([`ledger,${orgId}\n`], { type: "text/csv" });
}

Tune It

Replace <lang> with python, javascript, typescript, or rust.

[smells.<lang>.rules.stub_shipped]

action = "warning"
markers = ["not implemented" # thrown-error messages that mark a stub, matched as whole words
Default enabled state LanguageEnabled by default PythonYes JS / TSYes RustYes

docs.title: Weak Test Oracle (weak_test_oracle)
docs.text:
What it is

A test has no direct assertion, matcher, or expected exception — check whether it verifies behavior or only executes code.

Why it's bad

A test that only executes code can pass when behavior is wrong.

Example

PythonJS / TS

Problem

def save(value: int) -> int:
    return value


def test_saves() -> None:
    saved = save(1)
    save(saved)

Proposed fix

Assert an observable result or expected exception.

def save(value: int) -> int:
    return value


def test_saves() -> None:
    assert save(1) == 1

Problem

import test from "node:test";

function save(value: number): number {
  return value;
}

test("saves value", () => {
  save(1);
});

Proposed fix

Assert the result, state, or expected rejection with a matcher.

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";

function save(value: number): number {
  return value;
}

test("saves value", () => {
  assert.equal(save(1), 1);
});

Tune It

Replace <lang> with python, javascript, typescript, or rust.

[smells.<lang>.rules.weak_test_oracle]

action = "warning"
assertion_functions = ["expect*", "assert*", "verify*"] # globs for imported helpers that count as checks

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
The GitHub Action is the PR-facing wrapper for Sensez's feedback. It is useful when you want structural review comments or annotations without requiring every contributor to install Sensez locally.

The canonical action docs live in action/README.md, and the exact inputs are defined in action.yml.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
• Scans the repository path you pass in path.
  • Emits non-blocking annotations by default.
  • Adds inline review comments when with-comments: true.
  • Fails the job when fail-on-new is set and the findings meet that action level.
  • Uses the level input to choose the annotation severity.

docs.title: Minimal Usage
docs.text:
name: Sensez

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  sensez:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: popov95s/sensez@v1
        with:
          with-comments: false

docs.title: Blocking Mode
docs.text:
- uses: popov95s/sensez@v1
  with:
    with-comments: true
    fail-on-new: must_fix

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description path . Repository-relative path to scan. version latest Sensez PyPI version to run. threshold Optional duplication token threshold. with-comments false Add inline PR review comments. fail-on-new Fail when duplication meets this action level. level warning Annotation level: notice, warning, or error.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• pull-requests: write is only needed when with-comments: true.
  • The action is currently duplication-focused, so it is best used as the PR wrapper around the noze workflow rather than as the full docs surface for every pillar.

docs.title: MCP and Agents
docs.text: Sensez is designed to sit in the middle of an edit loop, not just at the end of CI. The MCP server is the integration point that lets a coding agent scan repeatedly during a session.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: There is nothing to run by hand. sensez init registers the server with your coding agent — Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi are supported — and the agent launches it automatically at startup. See Getting Started.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• noze_sniff — scan the repository for duplication, dead code, cycles, boundary violations, and smells. Takes an absolute repository root as path. Results are diff-focused by default (findings touched by uncommitted changes, computed over the full graph); pass diff=false for a full audit and limit to cap findings per pillar.
  • noze_gate — experimental end-of-turn diff gate, intended for hook integration rather than direct calls. May be noisy on short or Q&A turns. The Stop hook from sensez init --gate passes stop_hook_active, so the gate blocks at most once per stop chain, and waits up to 600 s, the server's own request limit, so a slow scan is not cut off into a silent allow. The gate blocks a finding once per session unless it is fixed and then reintroduced, which is reported as a regression. Its memory lives in .sensez/gate/, separate from metrics, and expires after seven idle days.
  • noze_explain — explain a finding category in plain English.
  • get_configuration_summary — summarize the effective configuration and the noisiest rules, as a starting point for tuning.
  • brainz_report — summarize local-only usage and resolution metrics.
  • brainz_triage — record the user's debt or false-positive verdict on a finding.

docs.title: Use In A Session
docs.text:
The important habit is to keep feedback close to the edit:

  1. Run a diff-scoped scan when the change is still fresh.
  2. Surface only the findings that matter for the current turn.
  3. Record debt or false positives when a finding is real but intentionally not being fixed now.

docs.title: Pair With CI
docs.text: Use the MCP workflow for immediacy, and keep CI for enforcement. The agent loop should be fast and conversational; CI should be the slower, stricter back stop.

docs.title: Affected tests with Reflexez
docs.text:
Reflexez runs the repository's existing pytest, Vitest, or Jest installation. It builds an impact plan and passes ordinary test-file paths to the runner.

Vitest already provides --changed and Jest provides --findRelatedTests; pytest core provides path/name filters and cached-failure selection, but not changed-source dependency selection. Reflexez adds one runner-independent workflow across all three: Git change-scope handling, transitive cross-file impact, computed dynamic-import analysis, explainable JSON plans, and conservative full-suite fallbacks. No test config, plugin, fixture, or runner command needs replacing.

sensez reflexez .

By default the change scope includes staged, unstaged, and untracked files; in a repository without commits every file counts as changed. For a branch or CI job, select an explicit base:

sensez reflexez . --base origin/main

--base adds the commits since the merge-base; staged, unstaged, and untracked files are still included, so a local run also covers uncommitted edits.

docs.title: Inspect before executing
docs.text:
sensez reflexez . --plan
sensez reflexez . --plan --json

Every selected file includes a reason (changed_test, direct_dependency, transitive_dependency, dynamic_import, full_requested, safety_fallback) and a dependency distance: the number of import hops from a changed file. A dynamic_import selection reached through a file whose computed import could not be resolved counts that file as one hop, since the import may load any module. The JSON plan also lists:

  • config_warnings: runner-config keys that could not be read statically, with the file, key, reason, and the fallback used for that key;
  • opaque_import_files: files whose computed imports could not be resolved;
  • unmapped_changes: changed files that exist but are not in the import graph (for example an asset nothing imports), so "0 tests" is never silent.

docs.title: Runner integration
docs.text:
Reflexez detects Vitest and Jest from each package.json: a script that runs vitest or jest selects that runner (both, when scripts run both); otherwise a vitest or jest dependency does, Vitest first. Without either in any package.json, a vitest.config.*, vitest.workspace.*, vite.config.* with a test key, or jest.config.* at the root selects the runner. A package.json that is not valid JSON is skipped with a config warning, and a runner project with no discovered tests is not run.

pytest tests follow the repository's pytest.ini, pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options], tox.ini or setup.cfg: its testpaths and python_files decide what is collected. When the repository root has none, the nearest such file above each test applies instead and pytest runs from its directory (for example backend/pyproject.toml). Without any, the default test_*.py / *_test.py patterns apply from the repository root. Force a runner only when auto-detection is ambiguous:

sensez reflexez . --runner pytest
sensez reflexez . --runner vitest

Arguments after -- are forwarded unchanged:

sensez reflexez . -- --maxfail=1      # pytest
sensez reflexez . -- --reporter=dot   # Vitest

Narrowed Vitest and Jest runs add --passWithNoTests, and a narrowed pytest run treats exit code 5 (no tests collected) as success. Full runs keep the runner's default, so an empty full suite still fails.

docs.title: Runner configuration
docs.text:
Reflexez reads Vitest and Jest configs statically (it never runs Node) to learn which files are tests and which files are shared setup:

  • Vitest: vitest.config.*, else vite.config.* (the test key), plus vitest.workspace.* and test.projects. Keys: include, exclude, setupFiles, globalSetup, root, dir. Project entries may be inline objects (with extends), config paths, directories, or globs with ! negations.
  • Jest: jest.config.*, else the package.json "jest" key, plus projects. Keys: testMatch, testRegex, testPathIgnorePatterns, roots, rootDir, setupFiles, setupFilesAfterEnv, globalSetup.

Supported config shapes: export default / module.exports objects, defineConfig/defineProject/defineWorkspace with an object or a function returning one, mergeConfig(a, b) (a relatively imported base config is followed), module-level const indirection, string concatenation and templates, spreads of local arrays and configDefaults.exclude, and path.resolve(__dirname, ...). Missing keys use the runner defaults.

A key that cannot be read (for example a helper call, an environment conditional, or a non-relative import) is reported as a config warning, and only that key falls back: include/testMatch to the *.test.*/*.spec.*/ __tests__/ file-name heuristic, exclude to the runner default, setup keys to no setup tracking. With --strict-dynamic, any such warning widens to a full run.

Use explicit paths in editor and staged-file integrations:

sensez reflexez . --changed-file src/service.ts

A relative --changed-file is resolved against the current directory, or against the repository root when no such file exists there (a deleted file).

docs.title: Safety model
docs.text:
Reflexez runs the full suite when a narrow plan cannot be proven safe. Current global triggers include:

  • dependency manifests and lockfiles;
  • pytest configuration and conftest.py;
  • Vitest/Jest configuration;
  • Sensez configuration and conventionally named test setup/environment files (setupTests.*, test-setup.*, .env.test*);
  • the configured setupFiles, setupFilesAfterEnv, and globalSetup modules, or anything they import;
  • TypeScript module-resolution configuration;
  • deleted or renamed source files (a rename counts as a deletion of the old path, including case-only renames); deleting other files, such as a README, does not trigger it;
  • incomplete parsing of a file that may import something (a file whose text has no import, require or from only triggers it when it changed).

Literal import(), CommonJS require(), importlib.import_module(), and __import__() targets use the normal import graph. Reflexez additionally resolves simple constant indirection, concatenation, template/f-string patterns, and import.meta.glob patterns, including arrays with ! negations and tsconfig path aliases. Static imports of assets (.css, .json, .svg, ..., including ?raw/?url suffixes and aliases) are edges too, so changing an asset selects the tests that import it. Assets loaded through new URL(...) or filesystem reads are not tracked. This work is isolated to the reflexez command; ordinary noze scans do not invoke the dynamic-import pass.

The plan always lists files with opaque computed imports. An opaque import in a file can load any module, so when source files change, reflexez also selects the tests that can execute that file (or the file itself when it is a test). Opaque imports in tooling that no test reaches do not widen the plan. Use --strict-dynamic in high-assurance CI to run the full suite on any opaque computed import, unreadable runner-config key, or changed source file outside the import graph:

sensez reflexez . --base origin/main --strict-dynamic

Full runs, from --full or a safety fallback, invoke each runner once in its root with no file arguments, so the runner's own discovery decides what runs. --full is useful for validating the integration:

sensez reflexez . --full

Reflexez intentionally does not enable unsafe runner optimizations such as disabling Vitest isolation or automatically adding pytest-xdist. Runner-level parallelism can change fixture, process, and shared-resource semantics; pass those options explicitly after measuring them in the repository.
